messages:
maria: Quick postmortem follow-up from the canary last night — it rolled back manually after 12% error rate. We flagged a few recurring patterns (latency spike under burst, config edge-case for multipart payloads). Need concrete action items for rollout hardening (auto-rollback, blast-radius caps, faster detection).
kevin: thanks — can you paste the timeline + what triggered manual rollback?
maria: timeline: start 23:12, first errors 23:17, 50% of errors by 23:20, ops decision to rollback at 23:25. The trigger was error-rate > 5% sustained for 3 mins + endpoint 500s increasing.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout "canary/feature-serve-v2" started by kevin at 1718999950. Auto-rollback: OFF. Manual rollback executed at 1719001500.
anya: recurring pattern note: we've seen multipart payload degradation in 3 incidents YTD — likely KV cache invalidation + batching interaction. We should add canary tests for large multipart sizes.
kevin: proposal from my side: implement auto-rollback config with these knobs: max_error_pct, min_duration, max_blast_percent. Also a soft-fail that drains traffic if threshold hit for 1 minute instead of full rollback.
maria: sgtm. initial suggested thresholds: max_error_pct=5, min_duration=120s, max_blast_percent=10%
samir: I'll own blast-radius enforcement in the router. Plan: enforce max_blast_percent at routing layer for canaries and add an emergency cap override that only SRE can toggle. Timeline: PR in 1 week, canary next week.
kevin: I'll own auto-rollback engine and the policy DSL. PR for engine + tests in 2 weeks. Needs a follow-up to add telemetry events: "canary.rollback.initiated" and reason tags.
maria: Anya, can you add targeted evals for multipart payloads and a synthetic that reproduces the latency spike?
anya: Yes. I'll add a daily synthetic that hits large multipart payloads and an integration test in the canary suite. ETA: 10 days.
maria: Also action: add a runbook paragraph for "canary shows rising latency > X and errors > Y" that tells oncall to toggle cap and call SRE. I'll draft it and tag you all.
kevin: small config example for reviewers:
```yaml
canary_policy:
  max_error_pct: 5
  min_duration_s: 120
  max_blast_percent: 10
  auto_rollback: true
  soft_drain: true   # reduces traffic in steps before full rollback
```
maria: love the soft_drain idea. Can we ensure rollout telemetry includes percent_traffic and last_healthy_ts?
kevin: yes, will add those fields.
anya: alerting: add a composite alert: canary_error_rate > 5% AND latency_p95 > 2s for 2m -> page SRE and runbook link.
samir: question: should we default auto_rollback=off for release branches and on for hotfixes?
maria: I'd prefer auto_rollback=on by default for non-production branches, and an overrides table for major releases. Let's make defaults explicit.
kevin: I'll add feature-flag gating for the policy so product can opt-out per release.
maria: Owners + TL;DR: kevin -> auto-rollback engine + telemetry (2w), samir -> blast-radius router enforcement + admin override (1w), anya -> synthetic + canary tests + alerts (10d), maria -> runbook draft + follow-up w/ product (3d).
anya: noted. Will document the synthetic test steps in the canary repo.
kevin: will open a tracking ticket and link PRs.
maria: I'll add these as postmortem action items and set weekly check-ins until closed. Assigning owners in the doc now.
deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: weekly-checkin (canary-hardening) starting 1719008400.
maria: thanks team. Small ask: for every PR add a short note referencing the incident id: INC-2026-042 so we can correlate.
kevin: will do.
samir: sgtm, taking the router work.
anya: sgtm.
maria: closing thread — will update the postmortem doc with timelines and owners. If anyone needs to reassign, ping me. :thumbsup:
